{{Short description|German mathematician and computer scientist}}
[[File:Ludwig Staiger (2010).jpg|thumb|Ludwig Staiger in 2010]]
'''Ludwig Staiger''' is a German [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]] at the [[Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg]].

He received his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from the [[University of Jena]] in 1976; Staiger wrote his doctoral thesis, ''Zur Topologie der regulären Mengen'', under the direction of {{ill|Gerd Wechsung|de}} and Rolf Lindner.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=65034}}</ref>

Previously he held positions at the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|Academy of Sciences in Berlin]] (East), the [[Central Institute of Cybernetics and Information Processes]], the [[Weierstrass Institute|Karl Weierstrass Institute for Mathematics]] and the [[Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg|Technical University Otto-von-Guericke Magdeburg]]. He was a visiting professor at [[RWTH Aachen University]], the universities [[Technical University of Dortmund|Dortmund]], [[University of Siegen|Siegen]], and [[Brandenburg University of Technology|Cottbus]] in Germany and the [[TU Wien|Technical University Vienna]], Austria. He is a member of the Managing Committee of the [[Georg Cantor Association]] and an external researcher of the [[Center for Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science]] at the [[University of Auckland]], New Zealand.<ref>[http://www.cs.auckland.ac.nz/CDMTCS/docs/extpeople.html CDMTCS External Researchers]</ref>

He co-invented with [[Klaus Wagner]] the [[Staiger–Wagner automaton]]. Staiger is an expert in [[Omega language|ω-languages]], an area in which he wrote more than 19 papers <ref>{{DBLP |name=Ludwig Staiger}}</ref> including the paper on this topic in the monograph.<ref>[https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783642638596 Handbook of Formal Languages]</ref> He found surprising applications of ω-languages in the study of [[Liouville number]]s.

Staiger is an active researcher in [[combinatorics on words]], [[automata theory]], [[effective dimension | effective dimension theory]],<ref>[https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/search/?search=Staiger Electronic Colloquium on Computational Complexity Reports of Ludwig Staiger]</ref> and [[algorithmic information theory]].  He has [[Erdős Number]] 2 via to [[Solomon Marcus]].
